concepts.why: The presence of an anterior mediastinal mass and mediastinal widening, along with systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss, are consistent with Hodgkin lymphoma.
The presence of an anterior mediastinal mass and mediastinal widening, along with systemic symptoms such as fever, are also consistent with Non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
The presence of a large pericardial effusion and fever, along with a prolonged history of intermittent fever, could be consistent with tuberculosis pericarditis.
The presence of a large pericardial effusion and an anterior mediastinal mass could be consistent with lymphoma-associated pericardial effusion.
The presence of an anterior mediastinal mass and mediastinal widening could be consistent with a mediastinal germ cell tumor.
The presence of an anterior mediastinal mass and systemic symptoms such as fever could be consistent with Castleman disease.
The presence of an anterior mediastinal mass, hepatomegaly, and systemic symptoms such as fever could be consistent with sarcoidosis.
The presence of a large pericardial effusion and fever could be consistent with infectious pericarditis.
The presence of a large pericardial effusion and fever, along with a prolonged history of intermittent fever, could be consistent with tuberculous pericarditis.
